findings.description: The bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration block, meaning objects are stored unencrypted by default (no SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS enforced), risking exposure of data at rest.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No 'acl' attribute is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource associated, so the bucket could default to or be changed to a publicly accessible ACL, exposing potentially sensitive reports data.
The bucket stores ledger exports (likely sensitive financial data) but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving data unencrypted at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, so model artifacts are stored without encryption at rest.
The bucket lacks a server_side_encryption_configuration block, leaving operational runbooks (potentially containing sensitive infrastructure details) unencrypted at rest.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without protection, increasing risk of accidental or malicious data loss, and combined with no versioning there is no recovery path.

The object is uploaded to a bucket with no default encryption and no explicit server_side_encryption parameter set on the object itself, so the vendor roster file (potentially sensitive) is stored unencrypted.
No versioning block is configured, so accidental or malicious overwrites/deletions of reports cannot be recovered, and this also removes a safeguard against ransomware-style tampering.
